utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This case is IT-95-8/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dusan Fustar and Predrag Banovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And may I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the Prosecution, we have Mark Vlasic, who is a legal specialist; Camille Bibles, who is a trial attorney; and myself, Jocelyne Bodson. I'm a senior trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Theodore Scudder. I'm here on behalf of the accused Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jovan Babic, an attorney from Novi Sad, a member of the bar of Vojvodina, and I'm appearing for Predrag Banovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We have a number of matters to consider and take a decision on in this Status Conference. I should say that the consideration of these matters has been greatly facilitated by the preparatory work that has been done by the senior legal officer and the parties. The first matter that I want to raise is the amendment of the indictment. The motion for amendment was filed in April. There were delays in preparing the B/C/S version; and for that reason, the Defence was given until Thursday, the 9th of May, to respond. We had a response on the 6th of May from the Banovic Defence, but to date, no response from the Fustar Defence. And for that reason, I have to ask Mr. Scudder: What is the explanation for the non-response? Will there be a response?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I return to Chicago on Monday, we'll make a final decision on that. There may not be a response. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are aware that you are out of time. Your response should have been in by yesterday, the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When there are delays like that, it sets back the entire proceedings. Mr. Scudder. Mr. Scudder, stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will give you until next week, Tuesday, to file a response in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next matter is the pre-trial brief. The date that has been set for this was the 31st of May. Madam Prosecutor, are we still going to have it on the -- by the 31st of May?

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You will remember that during the Status Conference of 11th of January and during the meeting with the senior legal officer, Ms. Featherstone, it was expressed -- we were asked to focus this trial on the crimes which are mentioned in the indictment and not general facts which are already reviewed and ruled on by the Tribunal in other cases so that we can make effective use of the Tribunal's resources, making sure at the same time that the accused have a fair trial. Therefore, we transmitted to the Defence, on the 16th of April, a list of 81 points that we would like to have their opinion about. And these points have to do with the factual events which constitute the basis of this case, and we're speaking about information that comes from judgements that were rendered previously by the Tribunal in cases the Prosecutor versus Tadic, the Prosecutor versus Kvocka, and the Prosecutor versus Sikirica et al., which is also known as the "Keraterm I" case as opposed to the case that we're reviewing today and which is known as "Keraterm II." We met with the Defence counsel about this on the 8th and 9th of May, and I can tell you that communication between us was very good. Mr. Babic agreed with many of the points which we submitted, and we are waiting for the final response from Mr. Scudder today after this hearing. The Defence position, obviously, is decisive for the preparation of our pre-trial brief which we will file, as you mentioned in January, at the end of May. Obviously, it is very important for preparing that brief for us to know whether we can refer to the third amended indictment and the corrigendum which we filed with the Registry in April, and we would, on that point, like to have your opinion as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the information that you have provided. It is my hope that you will be able to file your brief by the 31st of May, and obviously, to do that, the final version of the indictment would have to be settled by that time. For that reason, the response from Mr. Scudder is all the more important. But we'll keep the 31st of May. In the event that you find that there is a need for an extension, you may apply, although I'm not inviting you. I'm not encouraging you to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, I forgot to mention that the list of facts about which there might be an agreement with the Defence will be appended to this pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We have next to look at a date for the filing of the Defence brief, and the date that I will set is Friday, August the 23rd. That is for the filing of the Defence briefs. The next issue I want to deal with is disclosure. First with respect to the requirements of Rule 66(A)(i). My information is that all the witness statements that accompanied the indictment on confirmation have been disclosed in both English and B/C/S without redaction. With regard to the requirements under 66(A)(ii), the Prosecutor has indicated that it will call approximately 25 witnesses in total. And I'm informed that translation and disclosure is progressing well. And it was expected that that would have been completed by the first week of May. Madam Prosecutor, can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As regards the requirement to disclose information under 66(A)(i), we have fulfilled our obligation. However, as regards disclosure of documents under 66(A)(ii), we were able to disclose to the Defence counsel the 17th and 18th of April all of the case file of the first trial, which we'll call "Keraterm," as well as more than 50 per cent of the documents in this case on paper copy as well as on CD-Rom in order to facilitate searches. As of the 19th of March, we asked the research department -- or search department to carry out additional searches in order to finish the disclosure obligation. Unfortunately, that section is currently completely taken up for searches for the Milosevic case in Bosnia and Croatia. And the deadline for the disclosure, as you know, is the 1st of June. This means that the searches in our case have taken on a slight delay. To that extent, we respectively [as interpreted] call your attention to a request for an extension of the time in order to fulfill our obligations under 66(A)(ii), and we would like to be able to finish this work by the 15th of June. As regards the list of the witnesses, for the time being, it is almost ready, and we have about 25 witnesses. As regards the list of exhibits, it, too, is almost complete, and there are about 20 exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you are asking for an extension to the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's possible, that would facilitate our work. If not, we will finish what we have to finish by the end of May as had been stated at the Status Conference of 11 January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll extend the time to the 15th of June. The next matter is the list of experts. The OTP had indicated it would be calling four experts: Forensic anthropologist, a forensic medical examiner, a member of the commission of experts - that's Dr. de Grave - and an investigator in relation to burial sites. The expert reports have been obtained and translated and were to be provided to the Defence at the time of the last Rule 65 ter conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They have been provided?

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the only testimony which will be in written form under 92 bis, we filed on the 20th of April a motion for that statement to be accepted. This is the statement of Dr. de Grave who testified during Keraterm I trial. As regards the rest, all other expert reports were transmitted to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. I have seen the application for 92 bis. And in due course, we should be ruling on that. Exhibits, I think you've already given the information with regard to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There are about 30 exhibits. The list is not completely ready, but we can certify that it will be ready by the end of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And as for 92 bis in general, my understanding is Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that you take the view, Madam Prosecutor, that most of the witnesses will testify as to the acts and conduct of the accused; and for that reason, Rule 92 bis would not be applicable?

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct, Your Honour. As you asked, we will focus on crimes and the conduct of the accused. And as regards everything with background, factual basis, context, and any possible expert reports on the general background of the war, we are hoping to reach an agreement with the Defence about agreed facts to which I referred to a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I encourage the parties -- encourage the Defence to work with the Prosecutor on the question of agreed facts. The length of the trial: Madam Prosecutor, you have about 20 witnesses. At the rate of one per day, it would seem that the Prosecutor's case should be completed within three to four weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think that that is what we can say, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask whether any of the Defence counsel is in a position to give, at this stage, a general indication as to the scope of the -- of the Defence case? Mr. Scudder?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: Judge, I really could not be very specific. My best estimate at this time is that if the Prosecution took three to four weeks, our witnesses wouldn't exceed two weeks. We have names and information from investigators. I have not personally interviewed the people, so the guess is a little bit rough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can also say for the time being, since we have not received all the material which we were supposed to receive from the Prosecution until the 15th of June, I cannot really say precisely how long the presentation of our evidence will last. But as far as I know, I don't think it will exceed two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I remind all the parties that we're working towards a target of being ready for trial within six months of initial appearance. So that's January (sic). The date of the next Status Conference, in terms of the requirements of the Rules, the next Status Conference will have to be held no later than the 5th of September. I'm going to fix Friday, the 30th of August, as the date for the next Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you permit. I would like to raise an additional point as regards possible protective measures for the victims and witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, we have a list of witnesses which are many of the witnesses in the Keraterm I trial. The Prosecution has filed a request for protection of witnesses, and Judge -- President Jorda, rather, granted the protective measures that were asked for on the 17th of April. But at the same time, he decided that new pseudonyms were to be given to the witnesses. We believe that this is a source of confusion, both for the witnesses themselves, the Judges, the Prosecution, and the Defence, and we would therefore ask that the same pseudonyms as those used during the first Keraterm trial, Keraterm trial I, be used in the Keraterm trial II. That is the case we are reviewing today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I can hear your submission. I can see advantages in the method suggested by the President. I think there are arguments on either side. We will have to consider this. We will consider this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask whether there is any matter that the accused or his counsel wishes to raise about his detention or any other matter relating to the preparation of the trial? Let me ask the accused first. Mr. Banovic, stand. Is there any matter that you wish to bring to the attention of the Court, any matter concerning your detention, your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the Detention Unit, everything is all right, but my condition of health isn't really good. So I would like to have more attention paid to my health. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, are you in a position to elaborate on that, the matters relating to his health?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at the last Status Conference, I spoke about the need of providing appropriate medical care to my client in the Detention Unit. In contacting with my client and during my stay in Holland this time, and as regards the doctors are concerned in the Detention Unit, nothing has really changed much. And therefore, I have written a letter to the secretariat, and I would like to call upon the Court to have Mr. Banovic be given adequate medical attention and, therefore, to make our client capable to attend all the trial sessions. I hope that the adequate measures will be taken and that we can resolve the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean by "adequate medical attention"? Is there a particular problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client suffers from kidney diseases, and according to the information I received from the doctors, specialists, I was told that he needs to be checked up on a more regular basis, and this using ultrasonic measures. So far, none of these check-ups have been done. I have approached the secretariat, and I hope that it will be a measure that will be implemented continually and that we will not have to go back to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The health of the accused is very important. I'm going to suggest to you, Mr. Babic, that you file a motion asking the Chamber to require that a medical examination, including an ultrasound, be carried out on the accused for this purpose. You should file that immediately. And in the motion, you will put in all the information and the data that you have that will allow the Chamber to make a decision on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I shall do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sit, Mr. Banovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there any other matter from any of the parties?

utterances.speaker: MS. BODSON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This hearing stands adjourned.
